briefings.title: LIVE: Christine Lagarde Addresses Markets After ECB Governing Council Meeting | DWS News | AF14
briefings.tldr: The European Central Bank (ECB) raised its three key interest rates by 25 basis points in a unanimous decision, aiming to stabilize inflation at its 2% target amid ongoing energy shocks and geopolitical conflicts.

briefings.title: Live - ECB Governing Council Press Conference - 10 September 2026
briefings.tldr: The ECB Governing Council raised its three key interest rates by 25 basis points on 10 September 2026, driven by persistent inflation pressures from the Middle East conflict and updated staff projections showing headline inflation at 3% for 2026, 2.5% for 2027, and 2.1% for 2028.

briefings.title: Full Discussion: Lagarde And Costa Discuss Europe's Future In High-Level Stage Conversation | AC1F
briefings.tldr: Europe is actively addressing its productivity and competitiveness gaps through a unified "One Europe, One Market" strategy and accelerated financial integration, aiming to establish strategic autonomy, streamline regulatory frameworks, and deepen capital markets in an increasingly volatile geopolitical landscape.

briefings.title: CNBC's Sara Eisen moderates a policy panel at the ECB Forum on Central Banking 2026 — 7/1/26
briefings.tldr: At the 2026 ECB Forum, central bank leaders from the ECB, Federal Reserve, Bank of England, and Bank of Canada signaled a coordinated shift away from rigid forward guidance toward "framework guidance," highlighting divergent regional economic pressures and the massive, hard-to-measure impacts of AI on productivity and financial stability.

briefings.title: Price stability in challenging times
briefings.tldr: Central bank leaders from the ECB, Fed, Bank of England, and Bank of Canada affirmed their shared commitment to restoring price stability, highlighting a collective pivot away from rigid forward guidance toward flexible, data-driven "framework guidance" to better navigate rapid economic shocks and structural shifts like AI.

briefings.title: ECB Governing Council Press Conference - 11 June 2026
briefings.tldr: The ECB Governing Council unanimously raised its three key interest rates by 25 basis points in response to persistent inflationary pressures driven by the Middle East conflict, maintaining a highly data-dependent, meeting-by-meeting policy approach without pre-committing to a specific rate path.

briefings.title: ECB President Christine Lagarde: Stablecoins within a Global Context
briefings.tldr: ECB President Christine Lagarde argues that Europe should not rush to promote euro-denominated stablecoins as a direct competitor to the US dollar; instead, the focus must be on building public infrastructure that places central bank money at the heart of digital settlement to preserve monetary sovereignty and financial stability.

briefings.title: WATCH LIVE: European Central Bank Press Conference with President Christine Lagarde
briefings.tldr: The ECB Governing Council kept its three key interest rates unchanged, adopting a strict data-dependent, meeting-by-meeting approach to return medium-term inflation to its 2% target amidst intensified geopolitical risks, rising energy prices, and slower economic growth.

briefings.title: Merz, Lagarde & Deutsche Bank CEO Speak in Berlin at BdB 75th Anniversary Banking Summit | AC15
briefings.tldr: European leaders and banking executives are calling for an urgent deepening of the European Capital Markets Union and radical structural reforms in Germany to maintain global competitiveness amidst relentless geopolitical shocks and energy supply risks.

briefings.title: Exclusive: ECB President Lagarde Speaks to Bloomberg
briefings.tldr: ECB President Christine Lagarde characterizes the current European economy as sitting between "baseline" and "adverse" scenarios due to significant energy shocks, asserting that the ECB will remain agile and data-dependent rather than committed to a pre-defined rate path.

briefings.title: Lagarde Says Europe’s Economy Has Slipped Below ECB Baseline
briefings.tldr: The Euro area economy has shifted below the ECB’s baseline and is currently tracking between its "baseline" and "adverse" scenarios due to significant energy shocks.

briefings.title: LIVE: Lagarde addresses the 'ECB and Its Watchers' conference at Frankfurt University
briefings.tldr: Facing renewed geopolitical risks in the Middle East, the ECB will employ a flexible, risk-oriented scenario framework to determine interest rate paths, prioritizing real-time data on wages, profit margins, and productivity over fixed timelines as it guides inflation back to its 2% target.

briefings.title: Christine Lagarde - President of the European Central Bank | Podcast | In Good Company
briefings.tldr: Christine Lagarde warns that the current global landscape mirrors the 1920s, characterized by transformative technological breakthroughs and geopolitical fragmentation; she argues that Europe must accelerate its green transition and AI integration to preserve its social democratic model amid demographic shifts and energy vulnerabilities.

briefings.title: ECB Governing Council Press Conference - 19 March 2026
briefings.tldr: The ECB maintained its key interest rates while signaling that the war in the Middle East has introduced significant uncertainty, leading to upward revisions for near-term inflation and downward revisions for economic growth.

briefings.title: Lagarde Reported to Leave ECB Before Term End, UK CPI Falls | The Opening Trade 2/18/2026
briefings.tldr: UK inflation data for January met headline estimates at 3.0%, fueling bets for a March Bank of England rate cut, while markets react to reports that ECB President Christine Lagarde may step down before her 2027 term ends to preserve institutional independence ahead of French elections.

briefings.title: All the Single Markets: Panel Discussion with Lagarde, Michael, Wildberger | MSC 2026 | BR24
briefings.tldr: Europe is facing a decisive moment where external geopolitical pressures and economic competition are forcing a shift toward deeper internal integration, specifically through the "Savings and Investment Union" and digital sovereignty, while simultaneously struggling against self-imposed regulatory fragmentation.
